title: A structural global growth slowdown is making productivity, investment, labor-force aging, trade, and policy space central to future social opportunity
source_unit: World Bank, Falling Long-Term Growth Prospects: Trends, Expectations, and Policies
geography: Global and regional potential growth across advanced economies and emerging market and developing economies

growth_speed_limit.value: Global potential growth is expected to fall to a three-decade low over the remainder of the 2020s at current trends

growth_definition.value: Potential growth is the maximum longer-term growth the global economy can sustain without igniting inflation

development_consequence.value: A persistent and broad-based decline in long-term growth prospects imperils poverty reduction, climate action, and other development objectives

observations.method: World Bank book synthesizing global and regional analysis of potential growth and its drivers using a comprehensive database of potential-growth estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The projection is conditional on current trends and policy assumptions; potential growth is not realized GDP, household income, welfare, or a forecast of every country or group.
observations.subgroup: Emerging market and developing economies, advanced economies, workers, firms, households, governments, and populations dependent on growth for poverty reduction and public investment.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower potential growth can coexist with improved well-being if distribution, public services, environmental sustainability, and non-market value improve; aggregate growth is not a complete social-outcome measure.

observations.period: 1990s to 2026; drivers of the structural slowdown

denominator.unit: World Bank long-term growth driver framework

productivity.value: Growth in total factor productivity has weakened

labor_force.value: The global labor force is aging and expanding more slowly

trade.value: International trade growth is much weaker than in the early 2000s

observations.method: Cross-country and regional analysis of potential growth and its underlying drivers over recent decades.
observations.uncertainty: The driver set identifies broad structural forces but does not imply a single causal decomposition for every country or establish how shocks and policy responses will interact.
observations.subgroup: Workers and firms in trade-exposed sectors, younger and older labor-force cohorts, countries with different productivity and investment capacity, and households affected by slower income growth.
observations.counterinterpretation: Slower labor-force growth can reduce some pressures and encourage automation, while weaker trade can support local resilience in some settings but reduce specialization, income, and technology diffusion.

observations.period: 2026; emerging market and developing economy implications

convergence_risk.value: Slower productivity, investment, labor-force, and trade growth can limit convergence and reduce the resources available for development

policy_burden.value: Countries must respond to lower growth while addressing poverty, climate change, income distribution, and other development objectives

global_support.value: National policy action is described as requiring cross-border cooperation and substantial financing from the global community

observations.method: World Bank global and regional assessment of structural growth prospects and policy options for advanced, emerging, and developing economies.
observations.uncertainty: The report’s policy routes do not demonstrate political feasibility, financing availability, distributional effects, or that cross-border cooperation will reverse divergence.
observations.subgroup: Low- and middle-income countries, governments with constrained fiscal space, workers, households, firms, and populations vulnerable to poverty, climate, and service shortfalls.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large investment push can raise productive capacity, but debt-financed or externally directed investment can deepen dependency, environmental damage, or inequality if local control and distribution are weak.

reversal_condition.value: The slowdown could be reversed by the end of the 2020s if countries replicate strong policy efforts from recent decades

investment_route.value: A major investment push grounded in robust macroeconomic frameworks is identified as a central response

policy_set.value: The policy response requires national action supported by cross-border cooperation and substantial global financing

observations.method: World Bank synthesis of evidence on potential growth drivers and policy options.
observations.uncertainty: The conditional reversal pathway is not a guarantee; it depends on investment quality, productivity response, labor and trade policy, macro stability, political capacity, and global cooperation.
observations.subgroup: Policymakers, investors, workers, firms, households, development institutions, and communities affected by infrastructure, climate, labor, and public-finance choices.
observations.counterinterpretation: Investment-led growth can expand opportunity, but it can also increase resource use, displace communities, concentrate firm power, or prioritize measurable output over social and cultural value.

boundary: This record adds a macro-to-social trend linking potential growth, productivity, investment, labor-force aging, trade, convergence, poverty, climate action, policy space, and global cooperation. It is a World Bank structural outlook, not realized GDP or household welfare, a respondent-level dataset, a causal decomposition for every country, or proof that investment-led policy will produce equitable opportunity.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official World Bank publication page reviewed for the three-decade-low potential-growth outlook, definition of potential growth, weakened investment/productivity/labor-force/trade drivers, development consequences, and conditional policy-reversal route.
